statements.venue: Letter from Luján alone to Senate leaders Thune and Schumer (dated 24 September 2026, released 28 September)
statements.quote: Researchers and leaders at top AI laboratories have also publicly raised the possibility of catastrophic outcomes, suggesting there’s a 10% to 20% chance of existential risks associated with these platforms.
statements.context: Luján was asking Senate leaders to create a bipartisan select committee on AI and listed the warnings that he said justify it.
statements.reason: He relays experts' warning of existential risk and in the next sentence says these warnings deserve full attention and that Congress should listen, while adding that Congress need not assume any prediction is correct, so the endorsement is qualified (between A and C).

statements.venue: Letter from Luján alone to Senate leaders Thune and Schumer (dated 24 September 2026, released 28 September)
statements.quote: At the same time, leading AI researchers and developers are publicly warning that this technology is advancing beyond our ability to reliably understand or control it.
statements.context: Same letter, describing why Congress needs a dedicated AI committee.
statements.reason: Relays a loss-of-control warning and treats it as deserving serious examination, without saying the loss would be permanent.

statements.venue: Letter from Luján alone to Senate leaders Thune and Schumer (dated 24 September 2026, released 28 September)
statements.quote: Just last week, Anthropic shared their threat intelligence report documenting AI-enabled cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, biological misuse, conventional weapons development, and increasingly autonomous attacks.
statements.context: Same letter; the preceding sentence, in his own words, says the threat landscape continues to broaden.
statements.reason: Cites a report of AI-enabled biological misuse and weapons development as evidence of a broadening threat, which is catastrophic-type misuse without extinction framing; the harms are listed rather than described as mass-casualty, so it sits near C.

statements.venue: Letter from Luján alone to Senate leaders Thune and Schumer (dated 24 September 2026, released 28 September)
statements.quote: AI is accelerating faster than our existing legislative processes, committee structures, and technical capacity can consistently evaluate and respond. The recent news of increasing incidents makes it clear that this is no longer a theoretical concern.
statements.context: Same letter; this passage is also the quote attributed to him in the press release.
statements.reason: His own words acknowledging serious risk from advancing AI in general terms.

statements.venue: Letter to President Trump signed by 17 senators
statements.quote: a formal agreement that would slow down, and potentially enact a mutual pause in, frontier AI development to prevent cyberattacks, the development of biological weapons, and other dangerous activities that threaten the lives of the American people and humanity writ large.
statements.context: The senators urged Trump to negotiate AI guardrails with Xi Jinping at the summit planned for 24 September 2026.
statements.reason: The letter he signed says AI-enabled activities threaten humanity as a whole, which is level A under ruling 1.

statements.venue: Letter to President Trump signed by 17 senators
statements.quote: While advanced AI may be new, engagement between two superpowers over a technology that poses an existential threat is not.
statements.context: Same letter, comparing AI talks with China to Cold War nuclear arms control.
statements.reason: The letter he signed calls AI a technology that poses an existential threat.

statements.venue: Letter to President Trump signed by 17 senators
statements.quote: The experts building frontier AI models have also been raising concerns for some time that the capabilities of AI models may soon accelerate beyond our ability to understand or control them.
statements.context: Same letter; a later sentence says "We should take these warnings seriously."
statements.reason: Relays and endorses a loss-of-control warning without extinction framing in this passage.

slowdown.note: Signed the 23 September 2026 letter calling for a formal agreement with China that would slow down frontier AI development to prevent catastrophic harms; his own 24 September letter (released 28 September) also cites, approvingly, AI company employees' call to deliberately pace frontier AI development.

pause.note: The letter he signed asks for an agreement with China that would "potentially enact a mutual pause" in frontier AI development; the pause is tentative and conditional on China joining. Evidence is a co-signed letter.

intl.note: Signed the 23 September 2026 letter urging Trump to negotiate a formal agreement with China to slow down, and potentially mutually pause, frontier AI development.

rsi.note: No statement found about banning self-improving AI. The co-signed letter mentions that automation of AI research may speed up progress but does not call for a ban.

record: Wrote alone to Senate leaders Thune and Schumer (letter dated 24 September 2026, announced 28 September) urging a bipartisan Senate Select Committee on AI, citing AI safety incidents and expert warnings of existential risk.
Text of the select committee letter as signed, dated 24 September 2026.
Luján letter (PDF on his Senate site), 2026-09-24
Signed the letter from 17 Senate Democrats, led by Van Hollen, urging Trump to negotiate an AI agreement with China, including a slowdown and possible mutual pause of frontier AI development.
Introduced, with Blackburn, Durbin, Risch and Welch, the TEST AI Act of 2025 to create federal testbeds at the standards institute and Energy Department for evaluating AI systems.
As ranking member, helped lead a Commerce subcommittee hearing on AI in communications networks; his quoted remarks were about broadband and competitiveness, not catastrophic risk.
With Heinrich and Rosen, wrote to Meta about antisemitic content on its platforms and in its AI models (outside this project's scope).
grade_reason: He signed the 23 September 2026 letter saying AI poses an existential threat and threatens humanity writ large, and the next day his own letter to Senate leaders relayed and took seriously lab leaders' estimate of a 10% to 20% chance of existential risk. The clearest A wording is from the co-signed letter; his solo letter's endorsement is qualified.

Carried over from the earlier run: the co-signed and solo-letter quotes were checked by program then as exact continuous passages of the downloaded page text (the first co-signed quote starts mid-sentence; the two A co-signed passages also appear on Luján's own release, re-confirmed this run). This run's page reads went through a summarising fetch tool, except the letter PDF, which I read directly. Grading judgment for review: the 10%-20% existential risk quote is a relayed warning whose endorsement is hedged ('not because Congress should assume any prediction to be correct'); I graded it A with the boundary flag, but a reviewer could reasonably make it C, which would not change the overall grade because of the co-signed letter.
